aria: Animated recap of the Sixers' 131 to 124 home win over the Pacers: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope's 3-pointer with 2 minutes 51 seconds left that made it 122 to 115, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Jaylen Brown's 31 points, the top scorers, how the Sixers won, and the next game at Brooklyn.
notes: Box score from the Philadelphia 76ers' 131–124 home win over the Indiana Pacers at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Nov 15, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with the SI.com play-by-play and game details from Field Level Media (via The Ticket), NBC Sports Philadelphia, Philly Sports Reports, Liberty Ballers (via Yahoo Sports) and Yardbarker. All 131 Philadelphia points and all 124 Indiana points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: 35–29 Indiana after one, 58–57 Philadelphia at the half, 97–87 after three. Team totals (field goals 47 of 85 to 48 of 91, threes 18 of 42 to 8 of 32, assists 29–32, fast-break points 20–7, points in the paint 48–62) are from the Covers box score. Biggest leads (Philadelphia 15, Indiana 9) are from the Covers box score; Field Level Media also has the 15, in the fourth quarter, and Yardbarker the 9. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games.

Philadelphia trailed 35–29 after one, took a 58–57 halftime lead on two LeBron James free throws in the final seconds, and won the third quarter 39–30 (Covers line score; Philly Sports Reports). Pascal Siakam scored 19 of his 31 in the fourth (Field Level Media; NBC Sports Philadelphia), and Quenton Jackson's layup at 3:17 cut it to 119–115 (SI.com play-by-play). Caldwell-Pope's three and Dean Wade's and-one dunk off a James pass at 2:27 made it 125–115 (SI.com play-by-play; Field Level Media). James finished with 15 points and 11 assists and passed Jason Kidd for third on the NBA's career assists list (NBC Sports Philadelphia; Philly Sports Reports). Philadelphia played without Joel Embiid (Field Level Media; NBC Sports Philadelphia). The Sixers play at Brooklyn on Monday, Nov 16 at 7:30 PM ET (Yardbarker).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Kentavious Caldwell-Pope's 3-pointer with 2:51 left, assisted by Tyrese Maxey, that made it 122–115 (SI.com play-by-play: three-point jump shot, Maxey assist, 115–119 to 115–122; Field Level Media: Caldwell-Pope's 3-pointer, then Wade's and-one, held Indiana off). The recaps don't describe the move, so it is drawn as the template's plain catch-and-shoot three from just behind the line. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Philadelphia 76ers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Caldwell-Pope's listed 6-foot-5 and 204 pounds (StatMuse, RotoWire), in Philadelphia's home white with No. 1 (StatMuse). No wingspan from a reliable measurement is reported, so his arms are drawn at a 1.0 ratio. He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn as a team-colour silhouette in the kit. It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
